review_notes: I read the whole file. It has two theorems. `common_access_gives_firstHeight_localization` is a thin wrapper around `bounded_firstHeight_localization` and the first theorem, so I found no repetition inside it. Within the file, the first theorem has no internally repeated block. I searched the SLE directory for repeats across files and found one: the intermediate-value argument that gives a strictly positive time where a continuous guide with β 0 = 0 reaches a given norm. It is repeated in at least three places, which I read in full: this file, GuideTipCollapse.lean and SmallImageSemicircle.lean. GuideSplice.lean and StripProbabilities.lean use related variants, and I did not count them. I could not compile anything, so the proposed lemma and its rewritten uses are untested sketches. The proposed lemma only helps if it lands in a shared file that all three modules import. I did not check the import graph to confirm which file that could be.

findings.problem: The proof first applies the intermediate value theorem to `‖β n ·‖` on [0, δ] to reach the radius b₀. It then shows the crossing time S is positive, because ‖β n 0‖ = 0 ≠ b₀. The same argument appears almost line for line elsewhere. In GuideTipCollapse.lean it is `obtain ⟨S, hS, hnormS⟩ := intermediate_value_Icc ht.1 hnorm hεmem` followed by `have hSpos : 0 < S`, with `hS0`, `rw` and `hε.ne'`. In SmallImageSemicircle.lean (`access_segment_section_anchor`) it is `obtain ⟨t, ht, htnorm⟩ := intermediate_value_Icc ht₀.le hβ.norm` followed by `have htpos : 0 < t`, with `heq` and `rw`. Each copy builds the membership `b ∈ Icc ‖β 0‖ ‖β T‖`, calls the IVT, uses `change` to restate the conclusion, and derives positivity by contradiction through `norm_zero`. Any change to this argument has to be made in three modules.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma to a shared geometry file that these modules already import. The lemma statement is `lemma exists_pos_norm_eq {β : ℝ → ℂ} {T b : ℝ} (hT : 0 ≤ T) (hβ : ContinuousOn β (Icc 0 T)) (hβ0 : β 0 = 0) (hb : 0 < b) (hbT : b ≤ ‖β T‖) : ∃ S, 0 < S ∧ S ≤ T ∧ ‖β S‖ = b`.

Proof sketch: apply `intermediate_value_Icc hT hβ.norm` with the membership `b ∈ Icc ‖β 0‖ ‖β T‖`, after rewriting `hβ0` and `norm_zero`. Use `change` to get `‖β S‖ = b`. Then show S ≠ 0, because S = 0 gives `0 = b`, contradicting `hb.ne'`. This yields S > 0 together with S ≤ T.

Use in `common_access_guide_radius`: replace lines 37-44 with `obtain ⟨S, hSpos, hSδ, hnorm⟩ := exists_pos_norm_eq hδ.le (hβc n) (hβ0 n) hb₀ hn.le`, then set `hsub := Icc_subset_Icc_right hSδ` and continue. Here `hS.2` becomes `hSδ`.

Use in `access_segment_section_anchor`: `obtain ⟨t, htpos, htT, htnorm⟩ := exists_pos_norm_eq ht₀.le hβ hβ₀ (Real.exp_pos v) hB.le`. The later `ht.2` is replaced by `htT`.

Use in GuideTipCollapse: take `hlarge : ε < ‖β n t‖` and apply the lemma on `Icc 0 t` with `ht.1`, `((hβ n).mono htT)`, `hβ0 n`, `hε` and `hlarge.le`. This also replaces the manual `hnorm` and `hεmem`.

The three rewritten uses keep the same hypotheses and imports; only `Complex`/norm basics and the intermediate value theorem are used.
findings.benefit: Three roughly eight-line copies of the crossing-time argument shrink to one-line calls. The positivity argument is stated and maintained in one place, with explicit hypotheses (`β 0 = 0`, `0 < b`, `b ≤ ‖β T‖`). In `common_access_guide_radius` the main proof is then just the choice b₀ = ‖z‖/2 plus the Lipschitz bound.
